analysis.title: US Utilities, Initiating coverage: Sustainable growth in a data centre frenzy
key_insights: HSBC initiates coverage of the US utility sector with 27 new stocks plus NextEra, 28 in total. It rates 18 Buy and 10 Hold.

The sector derated over the past three months as bond yields rose. The 10-year Treasury yield went above 5%, AI enthusiasm cooled and affordability concerns grew. The S&P utilities forward P/E fell to 15.98x at the low and has stabilised or recovered since the second week of October.

HSBC raises its US data centre electricity demand forecast to c900TWh in 2030 (+80%) and 1,800TWh in 2035 (+94%). Total US load grows 2.2PWh by 2035, a c50% increase on 2025. About two-thirds of that, 1.5PWh, comes from data centres.
US electricity demand is expected to grow 4-5% a year after roughly 25 years of flat demand. YTD 2026 growth is 2.4% and August was up 7.6% y/y.
Bottom-up, the coverage group's utility pipelines imply c170GW of new load by 2030 and more than 400GW by 2035. That compares with BNEF's data centre forecast of just under 200GW by 2035.

HSBC expects positive earnings revisions across the group as data centre deals signed in the last 12 months are written into business plans. Average 7-year TSR is 12%, from EPS growth of 8-9% and a 3-4% dividend and buyback yield.

Capacity build-out: renewables and storage additions rise from c50GW a year in 2024/25 to c80GW by 2030. Gas additions rise to 20-30GW a year by 2030, with c330GW over 25 years versus c200GW previously. Coal closures are cut to c50GW over 10 years from 100GW. Nuclear gains from uprates and extensions.
Electricity network investment in the coverage group almost triples (2.7x) by 2030 versus 2020. Gas network investment rises 1.6x.

Five themes: AIDC high growth (AEP, Xcel, NiSource, Sempra, Entergy, Evergy, NextEra, all Buy), AIDC compounders (Southern, PPL, Ameren Buy, with Duke, WEC, Alliant, CMS, DTE Hold), Generators (Constellation, NRG, Vistra, Talen, all Buy), Reform(ed)? (Pinnacle West, FirstEnergy, PG&E Buy, Edison Int. Hold) and Wires with overhang (CenterPoint Buy, Exelon, ConEd, Eversource, PSEG Hold).
Preferred stocks are Entergy, Pinnacle West, NextEra, NiSource, Sempra and the four IPPs. Top-quartile TSR of 14-16% is led by Entergy, Pinnacle West, Talen, NRG, Constellation and NiSource.
NextEra target price is cut to USD103 from USD114 but the rating is Buy, with 29.1% upside. HSBC cites the Dominion tie-up and NEER development growth.

NRG has the highest upside in the group at 72.5% (TP USD179). The thesis is pricing and contracting optionality, a 1.2GW hyperscaler framework agreement worth about USD500m of adj. EBITDA a year, and USD6.3bn of buybacks over 2027-30.

IPPs: nuclear tax credits give an inflation-adjusted floor of c45USD/MWh. PJM capacity payments add c14-15USD/MWh. Long-term nuclear PPAs run at c75+USD/MWh. HSBC models Constellation's implied nuclear price rising from the mid-40s in 2022-24 to the mid-80s in 2029/30.

PJM affordability is the main policy risk. Capacity prices rose to USD270 and then over USD300 per MW-day from c40. PJM plans a Reliability Backstop Procurement for c7GW with a 555USD/MW ceiling and c15-year contracts. HSBC says utilities are cautious on whether it works.

California wildfire legislation was not passed by 31 August. PG&E and Edison stocks fell over 20% and PG&E cut 2027 capex by USD2bn. HSBC rates PG&E Buy and Edison Int. Hold because Eaton Fire claims remain unclear.

Hold ratings reflect below-average growth or regulatory overhang. ConEd has the largest downside (-7.4%), followed by WEC (-2.0%). PSEG, Eversource and Exelon have limited data centre growth and political or regulatory risk.

Near-term catalysts: 3Q earnings and business plan updates from 21 Oct to 6 Nov, US midterms on 3 Nov, the Arizona Corporation Commission decision on Pinnacle West's rate case in December, PJM BRA 29/30 in December, the PJM RBP result in Dec 26 or Q1 27, and NextEra-Dominion approvals in Q4 26 or 2027.

HSBC's modelling implies US power sector CO2 emissions rise over the next ten years because of delayed coal closures and new gas, so zero carbon power by 2050 looks out of reach without hydrogen or carbon capture.

Valuation: regulated utilities are valued on 2027e P/E of 15x to 24x. IPPs are valued on EV/EBITDA of 9x to 16x. NextEra is valued on a sum-of-the-parts built mainly on DCF. The pan-US average 2026e P/E is 17.7x, with a 3.0% dividend yield.

sector_views.rationale: Fundamentals are the strongest ever, with 50% load growth by 2035 and a capex upcycle. The derating on higher yields is seen as partly offset by positive earnings revisions.
All four IPPs are Buy on scarcity pricing, nuclear contracting and buybacks. The average 2027e P/E is 13.1x versus 18.1x for integrated utilities.

sector_views.sector: Wires and pipes in the Northeast and California
sector_views.rationale: Affordability politics, regulatory overhang and wildfire liability keep ConEd, Eversource, PSEG, Exelon and Edison Int. at Hold.

earnings_insights: HSBC expects positive earnings revisions across the coverage group at 3Q26 and FY26 results as data centre deals enter business plans.
Pinnacle West: HSBC 2026e EPS USD4.72 and 2027e USD5.21 (estimates, EPS ongoing). 2026-30e EPS CAGR is 13%.
Entergy: HSBC 2026e EPS USD4.44 and 2027e USD5.11 (estimates). 2026-30e EPS CAGR is 13%.
Constellation: HSBC 2026e operating EPS USD11.98 and 2027e USD13.52 (estimates). HSBC and consensus EPS are above the top end of company-implied 2029 guidance.
NRG: HSBC 2026e operating EPS USD8.85 and 2027e USD11.97 (estimates). 2026-30e EPS CAGR is 19%.
Vistra: HSBC 2026e GAAP EPS USD9.03 and 2027e USD10.76 (estimates). 2026-30e EPS CAGR is 21%.
Talen: HSBC 2026e GAAP EPS USD23.72 and 2027e USD36.84 (estimates). 2026-30e EPS CAGR is 25%.
NiSource: HSBC EPS estimate is above the top end of company-implied 2030 guidance and consensus is at the top end.
PG&E: HSBC and consensus EPS are slightly below the lower end of company-implied 2030 guidance.
3Q26 earnings and business plan updates fall between 21 Oct and 6 Nov 2026.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The bond market rout drove the utility derating. HSBC fixed income expects yields to ease slightly by year-end and hold steady in 2027, which would help the sector.
This compares with 2020 and 2023 lows of 15.12x and 14.31x. It has shown signs of stabilising since the second week of October.
Demand is picking up as data centres connect.
After 25 years of flat demand, load is expected to grow c50%, or 2.2PWh, by 2035.

macro_indicators.reading: USD270 then over USD300 per MW-day
macro_indicators.interpretation: The price is 2.5-3x the 2015-21 average. It benefits IPPs and creates affordability pressure for regulated wires names.

macro_indicators.indicator: PJM wholesale power price incl. capacity and transmission
macro_indicators.interpretation: The range was 40-60 USD/MWh outside of price spikes.
IPPs expect higher ERCOT prices from 2028 under high-demand scenarios.

trade_ideas.rationale: Pricing and contracting optionality in Texas and PJM, a 1.2GW hyperscaler framework agreement and USD6.3bn of buybacks.
trade_ideas.risk: An extended pause to Texas data centre development could delay PPAs and depress forward prices.

trade_ideas.rationale: Top-quartile 13% EPS CAGR with Louisiana demand up c60% by 2030, in reasonably constructive regulation.
A year-end ACC rate case decision should remove regulatory lag and allow positive EPS revisions.
trade_ideas.risk: Execution risk is medium to high, given the history of adversarial regulation and an elected commission.

trade_ideas.rationale: 29.1% upside on NEER growth, the Dominion tie-up and a strong balance sheet.
trade_ideas.risk: Dominion tie-up approvals (FERC and states) in Q4 26 or 2027.

trade_ideas.rationale: One of the largest data centre pipelines relative to size, with a GenCo structure for execution.
Nuclear contracting upside, PJM capacity payments and nuclear tax credits.
trade_ideas.risk: Affordability pressure and PJM RBP could lower appetite for nuclear PPAs.

trade_ideas.rationale: Pricing and contracting optionality, with nuclear PPAs signed with AWS and Meta.
trade_ideas.risk: An extended pause to Texas data centre development could soften forward prices.

trade_ideas.rationale: Open positions give upside in PJM from 2028.
trade_ideas.risk: New-build CCGT economics in PJM remain challenging.

trade_ideas.rationale: Oncor Texas wires growth and 765kV opportunities.
trade_ideas.risk: Political scrutiny of data centres in Texas.

risk_factors: Rising bond yields reduce the relative appeal of utility dividend yields and raise financing costs, adding to affordability pressure.
Affordability concerns and political scrutiny may slow rate recovery and investment plans, especially in CAISO, PJM and the Northeast.
PJM capacity market failure or the RBP design could change IPP economics and regulated-utility affordability.
California wildfire liability legislation was not passed by 31 August. Eaton Fire claims for Edison Int. may exceed the wildfire fund's capacity.
Texas political scrutiny of data centre load and the quality of Batch Zero load commitments, which are letters of agreement rather than binding service agreements.
A delay or pause in data centre buildout would hurt demand growth and forward power prices.
Nuclear tax credits may not be extended beyond 2032 and nuclear PPA appetite could fall on affordability concerns.
Supply chain cost inflation for turbines, transformers and cables, which are up 2-3x or 200-300% since 2020-21.
Delayed coal closures and added gas push up power sector carbon emissions.
Rate case outcomes and credit downgrade thresholds on higher leverage.

tension_points.theme: utility derating versus data centre fundamentals
tension_points.bull_case: Fundamentals have never been stronger. HSBC expects 50% load growth by 2035 and positive earnings revisions as data centre deals enter business plans. P/E has started to stabilise.
tension_points.bear_case: Treasury yields above 5% hurt the relative appeal of dividends and raise financing costs. Affordability concerns increase regulatory and political scrutiny of rate recovery.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained rise in the 10-year Treasury yield, or a disappointment on earnings revisions at 3Q26 results (21 Oct to 6 Nov).

tension_points.bull_case: High capacity prices, nuclear tax credits and long-term PPAs de-risk nuclear earnings and lift IPP profitability.
tension_points.bear_case: Affordability pressure and PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement could lower appetite for nuclear PPAs. Politicians and governors are intervening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nuclear tax credits not extended beyond 2032, or the RBP and BRA outcomes in December 2026 or Q1 2027 weakening contracting.

tension_points.bull_case: Utilities and HSBC see political acknowledgement that reform is needed and expect passage in 2026 or 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: The package failed on 31 August, stocks fell over 20%, PG&E cut capex and Eaton Fire claims for Edison remain unclear.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Passage of wildfire liability legislation in a Q4 2026 special session or by the new governor and legislature from January 2027.
